item.title: Mendi Munhiu prioritizes maternal health care
item.description: Six new maternity wings have been established across health centers in the Mendi-Munhiu district in Southern Highlands province. The improved facilities will provide health workers with a more suitable environment to conduct antenatal checks, monitor pregnancies, assist with deliveries and respond to complications.
item.content:encoded:
Six new maternity wings have been established across health centers in the Mendi-Munhiu district in Southern Highlands province.

The improved facilities will provide health workers with a more suitable environment to conduct antenatal checks, monitor pregnancies, assist with deliveries and respond to complications.

Mendi Munhiu, MP Raphael Tonpi said the first of the new maternity facilities at Topa Health Centre in Karinz local level government, has already been completed and commissioned.

“Every mother deserves safe and quality health care, regardless of whether she lives in town or in a remote village,” he said.

Each of the six health centres will also be supported with a brand-new ambulance to strengthen emergency referrals and ensure mothers and other patients can be transported quickly to higher-level health facilities when necessary.

Mr Tonpi said the maternity facilities are developed through a partnership between the District’s Development Authority and the Provincial’s Health Authority.

He said K300,000 has been allocated to each maternity facility to support construction and improve the standard of maternal healthcare available in the district.

Mr Tonpi confirmed that the remaining four maternity wings are expected to be commissioned in the coming weeks at Munhiu, Wais, Pingirip and Mogol health centres.

item.title: Bougainville referendum results tabled
item.description: Parliament today witnessed the historic tabling of the 2019 Bougainville Referendum results, where 97.7 percent Bougainvilleans voted overwhelmingly for Independence. Minister for Bougainville Affairs Manaseh Makiba also tabled the Joint Consultation Report and the Melanesian Framework Agreement.
item.content:encoded:
Parliament today witnessed the historic tabling of the 2019 Bougainville Referendum results, where 97.7 percent Bougainvilleans voted overwhelmingly for Independence.

Minister for Bougainville Affairs Manaseh Makiba also tabled the Joint Consultation Report and the Melanesian Framework Agreement.

The former is a record of the joint consultations between the two governments following the Referendum while the latter outlines the way forward if the National Parliament affirms the majority vote.

While the three documents were tabled, there was no full debate on the three documents, especially the Melanesian Framework Agreement.

The PNG and Bougainville Governments wre unable to reach consensus on on a possible pathway in the event the National Parliament does not accept the referendum results.

Bougainville Affairs Minister Manaseh Makiba outlined that the Melanesian Framework agreement only caters to a vote by parliament, which is in favor of the referendum results.

He however reiterated that Parliament “retains the discretion to make any decision on the Referendum results as it considers appropriate.”

Makiba says in the event of a negative vote, a pathway can be carved out in line with the Bougainville Peace agreement:

Minister Makiba reminded members of the House of the enormous responsibility they have when they eventually vote on the referendum results, urging them not to forget the aspirations of Bougainvilleans captured in their referendum results.

item.title: Sandaun coin fund touching rural lives
item.description: More than 4,000 men, women, and children from the Vanimo-Green District are now members of the new Sandaun Coin Fund Business Association. The Association helps rural communities that banks and other services cannot easily reach.
item.content:encoded:
More than 4,000 men, women, and children from the Vanimo-Green District are now members of the new Sandaun Coin Fund Business Association.

The Association helps rural communities that banks and other services cannot easily reach.

"Sandaun Coin Fund Business Association is a community-based organization dedicated to improving the livelihoods of members through financial support, training, business development, agriculture, fisheries, and income-generating activities,” Association deputy chairman James Nakmai said.

The Association’s goal is to empower individuals, families and communities to become financially independent and economically productive.

Poultry and fisheries farmers in rural LLGs have been supported with chicklets, fingerlings, feed, and rice seedlings, 7 rice mills have been purchased and are ready to be sent to farmers so they can mill their own rice after harvest.

The first rollout of the SME loans will be given to people in the Imbio Census area on Friday 28th August 2026. Loans start from K500 and go down and are repaid on a monthly schedule.

Mr Nakmai clarified that loans and agricultural support are given with an agreement. Members must repay loans on time, attend meetings and training sessions, maintain honesty and transparency, and Support community development initiatives

The Association is also partnering with the churches, the education and health sector and the local communities to achieve its goals.

Established in September last year and now setting up its provincial headquarters office at Transmitter in Vanimo Urban, the Sandaun Coin Fund has been conducting awareness and registering members across all local level government areas in the Vanimo-Green District.

item.title: Dry spell threatens lives
item.description: Lives are at stake as food gardens and water sources are dying and drying in this prolong dry spell. While Western Highlands is known for being the "food basket" of PNG, this is not so anymore as ground becomes dry and dusty difficult for garden foods to grow and water becomes scarce.
item.content:encoded:
Lives are at stake as food gardens and water sources are dying and drying in this prolong dry spell.

While Western Highlands is known for being the "food basket" of PNG, this is not so anymore as ground becomes dry and dusty difficult for garden foods to grow and water becomes scarce.

People in Western Highlands Province are now starting to feel the real effect of this dry spell or Elnino roasting their food gardens and drying up their source of water for drinking, cooking, bathing, and general use.

One farmer of Hagen Central District at Kelam Village William Pupti said garden was his only source of survival.

Mr. Pupti said farming was helped him and his family built their permanent family hous3, helped pay for his children's schools fees and basically sustain him and his family's survival.

However, he added now with this prolong dryness, he and other members of his community cannot plant food especially in large quantity like sweet potatoes, cabbages, potatoes and or broccoli to supply markets.

" My family and I live on garden to sustain our livelihoods. I produce garden foods like cabbages, potatoes, and others in large quantity to supply markets in Lae, Pom and contract engagements with Highlands Fresh.

"That's when rain and sun accompanies each other. Now it hard to produce good food because the dryness has affected all our gardens and water sources," farmer Pupti stressed.

Also another farmer Andrew Kunjil spoke of the village's only source of clean water that has completely stopped flowing forcing locals to look for clean water.

" The only source of clean water that is pumped out from the head of the river has been affected, lowering the water pressure and eventually the water source dried up entirely, affecting almost a thousand users of the water.

"Now we are looking for water from the big rivers [which are also drying] and doing rationing, telling people not to fetch a large quantity of water, rather enough for use," farmer Kunjil elaborated.

This El Nino which is predicted to be the hardest around the months of September-November will surely had a tremendous negative impacts on the daily lives of the people of Western Highlands and calls are forwarded strongly to the DDAs and the provincial government and other stakeholders to seriously look into this natural catastrophe and find measures possible to help sustain the livelihoods of the people of Western Highlands Province.

And if Western Highlands the "food basket" of PNG is now faced with this truth of Elnino, PNG is at its vulnerable stage of collapsing unless government is serious about this phenomenon.

item.title: Vanimo marks national repentance day with call for faith, integrity and national renewal
item.description: Christian faithful gathered at the Pope Francis Oval in Vanimo today to observe National Repentance Day, with church and government representatives calling on Papua New Guineans to return to God, live with integrity and become agents of change in their communities. The annual observance on August 26 traces back to 2007, when then Prime Minister and Grand Chief Sir Michael Somare made a covenant de
item.content:encoded:
Christian faithful gathered at the Pope Francis Oval in Vanimo today to observe National Repentance Day, with church and government representatives calling on Papua New Guineans to return to God, live with integrity and become agents of change in their communities.

The annual observance on August 26 traces back to 2007, when then Prime Minister and Grand Chief Sir Michael Somare made a covenant declaration dedicating Papua New Guinea to God and calling the nation to repentance.

Representing the Council of Churches, Pastor Simon Surap said the national call for a government reset for the next 50 years must also recognise the need for God's guidance.

He said while the Government has plans to reset and reshape the country for the next 50 years, the success of those plans ultimately requires God and leaders who are willing to seek His guidance.

Pastor Surap urged Papua New Guineans to make repentance a way of life and not simply something observed on one day of the year.

Representing the Sandaun Provincial Administration, Acting Community Development Director Florence Agen called on the people, public servants and leaders to have the fear of God and to do what is right.

Agen encouraged the people to pray for the Government and the country's leaders, saying prayer is important in seeking God's guidance so that good things can happen in the country.

The observance at Pope Francis Oval included prayer, reflection and calls for repentance, with Christian faithful encouraged to examine their lives, turn away from wrongdoing and become the change God wants them to be.

However, the observance was also marked by a notable concern, the turnout was considerably smaller than expected.

Despite the Sandaun Provincial Administrator issuing a circular calling on public servants and stakeholders to observe National Repentance Day, only a relatively small number of people gathered at the venue.

The low turnout raises questions about how seriously the day is being embraced in the province, particularly given its purpose as a national day of prayer, reflection and repentance.

National Repentance Day is officially observed as a public holiday, but its intended message goes beyond simply having a day away from work. Previous national messages have emphasised that it is a time to humble oneself, seek forgiveness and commit to a change in conduct.

For those who gathered in Vanimo, the message was clear: Papua New Guinea's national renewal must begin with individuals, through faith, repentance, integrity, prayer and a willingness to do what is right.

As the country looks toward its next chapter, the call from Vanimo is for leaders and citizens alike to put God at the centre of their lives and work together to build a better Papua New Guinea.

item.title: El Nino top agenda
item.description: El Nino, its funding and preparedness was top of the agenda as parliament resumed this afternoon. Southern Highlands Governor William Powi asked a series of supplementary questions to Health Minister Dr Billy Joseph on El Nino prepardness, funding and its impacts on the health and education sectors.
item.content:encoded:
El Nino, its funding and preparedness was top of the agenda as parliament resumed this afternoon.

Southern Highlands Governor William Powi asked a series of supplementary questions to Health Minister Dr Billy Joseph on El Nino prepardness, funding and its impacts on the health and education sectors.

Western Highlands Governor Wai Rapa backed up his counterpart with similar questions.

The prolonged dry season is now having serious impacts on provinces with severe consequeses.

It is affecting communities, and health and education services.

Southern Highlands Governors William Powi says the country needs to know what the government is doing to assist the country at this time.

Govwrnor Wai Rapa told the house to declare it as a state of emergency and set up a task force to assist with the el nino impacts.

Health Minister Dr. Billy told the house he will provide detailed answers during this sitting as this an issue that concerns the whole country.

item.title: El Niño puts communities in Markham under severe pressure
item.description: Communities in Zumara, Marafau, Ngaruchaniang and Ngaruwapum in the Markham Valley are facing severe water and food shortages as prolonged dry conditions continue. Community leader Tony Kipu says the lack of rain is putting increasing pressure on families across the affected communities.
item.content:encoded:
Communities in Zumara, Marafau, Ngaruchaniang and Ngaruwapum in the Markham Valley are facing severe water and food shortages as prolonged dry conditions continue.

Community leader Tony Kipu says the lack of rain is putting increasing pressure on families across the affected communities.

“The biggest problem for our people is water. Our small streams and waterholes have dried up, and families are now forced to travel to the Umi River to collect water,” Kipu said.

He said men, women, and children are making the trip to collect water for drinking, washing, and other household needs, which would take up to thirty minutes before reaching the Umi River.

Kipu said the dry conditions are also affecting food gardens.

“Our gardens are suffering because there has been no enough rain. It is becoming difficult for people to plant and grow food,” he said.

Large areas of land across the communities have dried out and turned brown, while grass and crops are also showing signs of stress.

Kipu said farmers are particularly worried that continued dry conditions could lead to further food shortages.

“If this situation continues, our families will face more problems with food and water,” he said. He is calling on the government and relevant agencies to respond urgently to the needs of the affected communities.

“We are calling on the government to look at this situation quickly and provide assistance, especially with water and food,” Kipu said.

The situation highlights the vulnerability of rural communities in the Markham Valley, where many families depend on food gardens and natural water sources for their daily needs.

item.title: Many gather for national day of prayer in capital city
item.description: Thousands of believers turned out before sunrise this morning, packing Sir John Guise Stadium in Port Moresby for the National Day of Prayer and Repentance. Some arrived as early as 7pm last night and prayed through until morning, with the stadium filled with worship and prayer throughout the night.
item.content:encoded:
Thousands of believers turned out before sunrise this morning, packing Sir John Guise Stadium in Port Moresby for the National Day of Prayer and Repentance.

Some arrived as early as 7pm last night and prayed through until morning, with the stadium filled with worship and prayer throughout the night.

What set this gathering apart was the rare public alignment of political power and church leadership, with Prime Minister James Marape expected to deliver the keynote address shortly.

Several members of Parliament, including the Minister for Community Development, Youth and Religion, were already in attendance.

The event carries the theme "Resetting PNG Today for a Better Tomorrow in Jesus Christ," drawing on the words of Leviticus 25:10 [NIV]: "Consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee for you; each of you is to return to your family property and to your own clan."

Major church bodies used the occasion to openly name the nation's wounds, corruption, violence, economic hardship, and the need to protect the next generation.

A nationwide chain of prayer began after the speeches, at 8am, with several church leaders who took turns in prayer.

The program was organised by the Department of Community Development, Youth and Religion, in partnership with the PNG Council of Churches.
